newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end steady, focus on Endesa, Telex.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end steady, focus on Endesa, Telex.

text.p: Chilean blue chips ended a shade lower in highly volatile trade with attention focussed on swings in power giant Endesa and long-distance telecom Telex, said traders.
The bolsa is seen opening stable with no news expected to move individual stocks sharply, said Guillermo Tagle, head of research at Santander Investments.
"The fact the market ended unchanged after such erratic trade confirms that its stable at current levels," said Tagle.
The 40-share index, which had fallen 0.5 percent midday, closed down 0.08 percent at 115.33 pesos.
The general .IGPA index lost 0.1 percent to 5,340.48 pesos amid volume of 11.3 billion pesos.

For much of the day the bolsa tracked swings in Endesa which opened sharply lower on news that the firm had been accused by the World Bank of not fulfilling environmental commitments at its controversial Pangue and Ralco dam projects.
The stock recovered in afternoon trade with investors taking the view that the dispute was political rather than financial, said Tagle.
"There are many local groups which are pressurizing to stop Endesa building more dams on the Bio Bio," said Tagle.
"Investors don't think there's any risk that they won't go ahead with Ralco, although the firm may have to produce another report."
Pangue started operating last year and Ralco is under construction.
Endesa ended up 0.2 percent at 251-1/2 pesos.
Telex stock was suspended temporarily mid-afternoon after it climbed 13 percent in speculative trading. It fell back after dealing resumed to close up 3.45 percent 1,200 pesos.
While the stock was suspended, Telex issued a statement saying it was about to be granted a PCS mobile telephone licence and hoped to form a pact with a strategic partner.

Losers included financial holding group CruzBlanca, down 3.17 percent at 122 pesos and department store chain Almancenes Paris which shed 3.14 percent to 370 pesos. ((-- Margaret Orgill, Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595x212))
